title: runtime/edge: handle streaming client disconnects gracefully + keepalive tuning
author: Mateo Alvarez
body:
Context: We’ve had a recurring escalation pattern around intermittent streaming disconnects (customer sees stream end / connection reset; we sometimes record this as 5xx and keep generating tokens server-side until max_tokens). This shows up as elevated error rate + wasted GPU time during bursts, and makes triage noisy.

This PR makes streaming cancellation explicit and cheap:
- Detect client disconnect earlier in the edge streaming loop and propagate a cancellation to the runtime generation task.
- Treat disconnect as a normal termination path (logs at INFO + metric), not as an internal error (no 5xx emission when the client went away).
- Tune HTTP keepalive ping cadence for SSE to reduce idle timeouts on certain proxies without increasing per-connection overhead.
- Add metrics + tracing tags to distinguish: (a) client_disconnect, (b) upstream_timeout, (c) server_error.

Why now: Tied to SUP-4921 (enterprise, us-east) and the Escalation Playbook / known-issues sprint work (ENG-2841/2844). Support is asking for clearer signals and a validated workaround; this makes the server behavior more robust and reduces false ‘server error’ classifications.

Implementation notes:
- Edge: When write() fails / request context closes, call cancel_token.cancel("client_disconnect").
- Runtime: Generation loop now checks cancel token between decode steps and on batch boundaries; cancellation triggers a fast path that (1) frees KV cache blocks, (2) removes the request from the continuous batching scheduler, and (3) emits a final span event.
- Logging: Downgrade noisy error-level logs for ECONNRESET / broken pipe to debug, with structured fields: request_id, model, region, disconnect_reason.

Testing:
- Added unit test for cancellation propagation (mocked transport closes mid-stream).
- Added integration test that verifies we do not emit a 5xx when the client disconnects and that runtime stops decoding within a bounded time.

Rollout plan:
- Guarded via config flag: edge.streaming.graceful_disconnect_cancel (default: ON for hosted, OFF for private until validated).
- Deploy canary to us-east (10%) for 24h and monitor: streaming_disconnect_rate, decode_waste_tokens, 5xx_rate (stream endpoints), and scheduler queue depth.
- If stable, roll to 100% hosted; follow up with Private Deployments enablement note after validating with one private staging cluster.

Release note (internal): Streaming endpoints now cancel generation promptly on client disconnect and no longer misclassify disconnects as server errors; improved keepalive behavior and observability.

conversation:
Sean Gallagher (review): Can we be sure we’re not masking legitimate server-side failures as disconnects? We don’t want to undercount 5xx.

Mateo Alvarez (author): Good call. We only take the disconnect path when the request context is closed OR the transport write returns a broken-pipe/ECONNRESET. Server errors still go through the existing error mapping and emit 5xx. I also added a metric label stream_end_reason so SRE can validate distribution post-rollout.

Rafael Mendes (review): Please ensure canceling a request removes it from batching quickly. We’ve had cases where the batch holds onto a canceled req until next step.

Mateo Alvarez (author): Updated runtime/src/scheduler/continuous_batching.rs to check the cancel token at (1) admission, (2) before each decode step, and (3) when compacting the active set. Added an integration assertion that decode stops within 250ms on disconnect.

Allison Grant (review): Observability nit: metric names should follow the runtime.* namespace and avoid high-cardinality labels. request_id should not be a label.

Mateo Alvarez (author): Fixed. request_id stays in logs/traces only; metrics use {region, model_family, reason}. Renamed metric to runtime.streaming.end_reason_count.

Noah Patel (review): Keepalive defaults: can we confirm this doesn’t increase egress materially?

Mateo Alvarez (author): Default ping is 15s for SSE only (was 5s in some clusters due to a stale override). So this should reduce chatter. I left it configurable per region.

CI note: The first integration run failed due to a flaky timeout on the streaming test (too tight). Relaxed threshold and reran; green.

Sean Gallagher (final): Approved with rollout guardrails. Please post in #eng-oncall once canary is live and include which dashboards to watch.

Mateo Alvarez (author): Will do. Canary plan included in description + runbook link updated.

Merged via squash after approvals.
release_notes: Streaming stability: promptly cancels generation when the client disconnects; avoids misclassifying disconnects as 5xx; keepalive tuning for SSE; added metrics to separate client disconnects vs timeouts vs server errors.
